# §7 Peer Benchmarking — Highlights

## Highlight Candidates

1. **Data & Operational Health is the standout dimension** — scoring 82 vs. a peer median of 70 among other Furniture manufacturers, placing Jonathan Charles in the top 40%. Well-maintained product data and consistent import operations provide a foundation that most peers have not matched. [→ §peer]

2. **Four of five scored metrics fall in the bottom quartile** — value delivery (10 vs. median 60), adoption (33 vs. 75.5), trajectory (0 vs. 50), and catalog completeness (73.3% vs. 91%) all trail peers by material margins. These gaps reflect low platform activity intensity rather than missing capabilities. [→ §peer]

3. **Engagement is the nearest metric to the peer median** — at 50 vs. a median of 60, the 10-point gap is the smallest in the profile and the most actionable short-term lever for closing the distance to peer norms. [→ §peer]

4. **Feature breadth matches top performers** — all six benchmarked capabilities are active, including CPQ (11.5% peer adoption) and Kit Items (7.7%). Jonathan Charles has the platform infrastructure that the highest-performing accounts use; the gap is utilization intensity, not feature coverage. [→ §peer]

## Priority Action

- **Restart consistent platform usage to rebuild trajectory**: The trajectory score of 0 reflects zero eCat activity in the most recent quarter. Re-engaging reps with even a modest weekly ordering cadence would move trajectory, engagement, and adoption metrics simultaneously — the fastest path to closing multiple peer gaps at once. [→ §peer]
